6B.01.t: Anterior Approach to the Hip — Smith-Petersen & DAA
6B.01.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Smith-Petersen |
|---|---|
| Uses | DDH (developmental dysplasia of the hip) open reduction, head and neck fracture reduction, hemiarthroplasty, septic hip, tumour (Netter; AO) |
| Position | Supine, sandbag under the buttock (Hopp) |
| Incision | Front half of the iliac crest → ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine) → 8–10 cm down toward the lateral patella (Hopp) |
| Superficial plane | **Sartorius (femoral) / TFL (tensor fasciae latae; superior gluteal)** (Hopp) |
| Deep plane | **Rectus femoris (femoral) / gluteus medius (superior gluteal)** (Hopp) |
| Deep | Rectus direct head off the AIIS (anterior inferior iliac spine), reflected head off the rim → T capsulotomy (Hopp; AO) |
| Extension | Up the crest (pelvic osteotomy) · down the anterolateral femur (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.4 · 6B.01

- Find the gap **5–8 cm below the ASIS**, where the fascia thins; ER (external rotation) tenses sartorius (Hopp)
- Open the fascia **over the TFL** belly, not the gap → the LFCN stays medial (AO; Campbell)

### Dangers
| At risk | Where | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **LFCN** | Crosses sartorius ≈2.5 cm below the ASIS (Hopp; Campbell) | Fascia over TFL; cut → numb lateral thigh, neuroma |
| **Ascending LFCA** (lateral femoral circumflex artery) | In the TFL–sartorius gap ≈5 cm below the joint (Hopp) | Ligate; not too close to TFL → nerve to TFL within 10 mm (Grob 2015) |
| Femoral nerve | Medial to rectus (Hopp) | Stay lateral; feel the femoral pulse |
| Head blood supply | Superolateral neck (AO) | No retractor inside the capsule on the superolateral neck |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.5, 6B.6 · 6B.01

### DAA — the anterior THA version
- DAA (direct anterior approach) → distal half of Smith-Petersen, same plane (Campbell)
- Incision ≈3 cm distal and 3 cm lateral to the ASIS, 8–12 cm (Campbell; Sherif Khaled: 3 fingerbreadths)
- Retractor under **iliocapsularis** → shows the anterior wall and shields the femoral nerve (Sherif Khaled)
- Femur → release superior + inferior capsule only, **never the posterior structures** (Sherif Khaled)

| DAA ideal | DAA avoid |
|---|---|
| Primary hip, BMI <30, small woman, good bone, coxa valga (Sherif Khaled) | Neck fracture, protrusio, short neck, revision (Sherif Khaled) |

PITFALL — the deep plane of the DAA
- Hopp → rectus femoris / **gluteus medius** · Sherif Khaled → rectus femoris / **TFL**
- Both right → TFL lies over medius proximally; in the wound you retract TFL laterally
- Say → "**superficial sartorius / TFL, deep rectus / gluteus medius** — all femoral vs superior gluteal"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "anterior approach to the hip"
- Plane → sartorius + rectus (**femoral**) / TFL + medius (**superior gluteal**) → true internervous
- Open the fascia over TFL → LFCN safe medially
- Ligate the **ascending LFCA** in the gap
- Rectus heads off → T capsulotomy
- Danger list → LFCN, ascending LFCA, femoral nerve, head blood supply

6B.02.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Watson-Jones |
|---|---|
| Uses | THA (total hip arthroplasty), hemiarthroplasty, neck fracture ORIF (open reduction internal fixation) (Netter; AO) |
| Position | Supine, buttock over the table edge (Hopp) |
| Incision | 2.5 cm distal-lateral to the ASIS → over the greater trochanter → 5 cm below it (Campbell) |
| Interval | **TFL / gluteus medius** → both superior gluteal → no true internervous plane (Hopp) |
| Deep | Fascia lata behind TFL → vastus lateralis origin released → T capsulotomy (AO) |
| Extension | Anterior medius fibres or anterosuperior greater trochanter osteotomy (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9 · 6B.02

- Superior gluteal nerve enters TFL near its iliac origin → **stop short of the origins** (Hopp; AO)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Femoral nerve** | Most lateral in the femoral triangle → compressed by medial retraction (Hopp) | Anterior retractor tip on bone at 1 o'clock (right) / 11 (left) (Hopp) |
| Femoral vessels | Retractor pierces iliopsoas (Hopp) | Tip on the anterior rim |
| Superior gluteal bundle | Limits proximal extension (AO) | Stay distal |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.10 · 6B.02

CLINICAL PEARL — neck fractures: reduce, then fix
- Closed reduction → **Leadbetter** (flexion, traction, IR (internal rotation), abduction) or **Whitman** (extension, traction, IR, abduction) → check with the **heel-palm test** (Nagah p11)
- Cannulated screws → **inverted triangle**: two upper on the tensile side, one lower on the compression side (calcar) (Nagah p12)
- Subcapital → Smith-Petersen reduces only, fix through a second incision · basicervical → Watson-Jones reduces and fixes through one (Handbook)
- Child hip fracture → types 3–4 via Watson-Jones, types 1–2 via the anterior approach (Handbook)

PITFALL — is Watson-Jones internervous?
- Netter → "intermuscular" · Hopp → **no true internervous plane** (both muscles superior gluteal)
- Say → "**intermuscular, not internervous** → TFL and medius share the superior gluteal nerve"

6B.03.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Hardinge (transgluteal) |
|---|---|
| Uses | Primary THA, hemiarthroplasty for neck fracture (AO; Netter) |
| Position | Supine with the greater trochanter at the table edge (Hopp) or lateral (Abdel Azeem) |
| Incision | 5 cm above the greater trochanter tip → over the tip → 8 cm down the shaft (Hopp) |
| Interval | None → **split medius above, vastus lateralis below** (Hopp) |
| Deep | Anterior third of medius + minimus + anterior vastus lateralis lifted as **one sleeve** → capsule (Hopp; AO) |
| Extension | Distal only (split vastus lateralis) (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.11, 6B.12, 6B.13, 6B.14 · 6B.03

- Split medius at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two-thirds → posterior insertion stays (Netter; AO)
- Inverted-T tenotomy of the anterior medius; any capsulotomy (Abdel Azeem)

| At risk | Where | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Superior gluteal nerve** | Between medius and minimus **3–5 cm above the greater trochanter** (Hopp; AO) | Stay suture at the apex of the split; no traction (Abdel Azeem) |
| Transverse LFCA | Under vastus lateralis (Hopp) | Cauterise |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.15, 6B.16 · 6B.03

- Limp after the lateral approach → usually superior gluteal **neurapraxia** → avoidable (Abdel Azeem)
- Or a failed abductor repair → reattach the anterior flap through bone holes (AO)
- **Modified McFarland** → anterior third of medius + vastus lateralis as a sleeve → extensile for revision (Abdel Azeem)

PITFALL — how far up can you split medius?
- Hopp, AO → 3–5 cm · Campbell → ≤4–5 cm · Khaled Fawzy → 5 cm
- Abdel Azeem → lower third of the trochanter-to-crest distance
- Lowest branch can sit at 3 cm (Bos 1994; Basarir 2008) → 6A 6.11
- Say → "**split no more than 3–5 cm above the tip; tie a stay suture at the apex**"

6B.04.t: Posterior Approach to the Hip — Moore / Southern
6B.04.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Posterior (Moore) |
|---|---|
| Uses | THA, hemiarthroplasty, posterior dislocation, posterior wall (Netter) |
| Position | True lateral; posts on pubis + sacrum, not on the lumbosacral junction (Abo Elsoud) |
| Incision | 6–8 cm above-behind the greater trochanter, in the line of maximus → down the shaft 10–13 cm (Hopp; Campbell) |
| Interval | None → **split gluteus maximus** (supply enters far medially) (Hopp) |
| Deep | Flex + IR → rotators cut **close to the greater trochanter**, stay sutures, reflected over the sciatic nerve → capsule (AO) |
| Extension | Upper quadratus femoris, maximus tendon release (Hopp) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.17, 6B.18, 6B.19 · 6B.04

- Split maximus ≤7 cm above the greater trochanter → inferior gluteal branch to its upper part (Campbell)
- **Palpate** the sciatic nerve; never dissect it (Hopp; AO)
- Cut the posterior labrum with a knife, not diathermy → heat near the nerve (Abo Elsoud)

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Sciatic nerve** (peroneal division) | Lateral, little fat, tethered at the notch (Khaled Fawzy) | Knee flexed, hip extended for closure; no retractor on it |
| Inferior gluteal artery | Under piriformis → retracts into the pelvis (Hopp) | Bleeds → supine, internal iliac control |
| **MFCA** | Under quadratus femoris (Netter) | Keep quadratus + obturator externus when the head matters (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.20, 6B.21 · 6B.04

CLINICAL PEARL — repair the back wall
- Repair capsule + rotators through drill holes in the greater trochanter → fewer dislocations (AO)
- Old posterior approach excised the capsule → high dislocation (AO; Azzam)
- Repair to the medius tendon with non-absorbable sutures (Abo Elsoud)

PITFALL — how much lengthening is safe for the sciatic nerve?
- Khaled Fawzy → palsy risk above **2.5 cm** · Fouad Zamel (dysplasia) → above **3.5–4 cm**
- Say → "**over 2.5 cm starts the risk; beyond 4 cm in high dysplasia → shortening osteotomy**"; feel nerve tension at reduction (Fouad Zamel)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "posterior approach to the hip"
- No internervous plane → split maximus in its fibres
- Flex + IR → piriformis, gemelli + obturator internus cut near the greater trochanter, reflected over the **sciatic nerve**
- Keep **quadratus femoris + obturator externus** → MFCA
- T capsulotomy → dislocate in flexion + IR
- Close → capsule + rotators repaired → lower dislocation

6B.05.t: Choosing the THA Approach — Cup and Stem Landmarks
6B.05.b:
### Which approach?
| Approach | Strength | Weakness |
|---|---|---|
| **Posterior** | Easy, extensile, revision, obese (Abo Elsoud) | Dislocation if not repaired |
| **Direct lateral** | Lowest dislocation → elderly fracture (Abo Elsoud) | Limp (superior gluteal nerve, abductor repair) |
| **DAA** | Muscle sparing, fast early recovery (Sherif Khaled) | Learning curve, LFCN, femoral fracture ≈2.5% (Abo Elsoud) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.22 · 6B.05

- Dislocation → posterior ≈10× lateral and 2× DAA · equal after 2007 once the back wall is repaired (Abo Elsoud)
- Instability ≈3% of primaries → 75% in the first year → ≈8% after spinal fusion (Azzam)

### Templating numbers
| Number | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Dorr ratio** (canal 10 cm below LT (lesser trochanter) ÷ at LT) | A <0.5 cementless · B 0.5–0.75 · C >0.75 cemented | Handbook |
| **Lewinnek safe zone** | Anteversion 15 ± 10° · inclination 40 ± 10° | Azzam |
| **Combined anteversion** | 30–50° | Azzam |
| Cup template | 45°, medial edge on the ilioischial line, lower edge at the teardrop | Handbook |
| Neck cut | Greater trochanter tip → 1 fingerbreadth above the LT | Handbook |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.23, 6B.24 · 6B.05

- Sitting → pelvis tilts back 20–35° → cup anteversion rises; stiff or fused spine → dislocates sitting (Azzam)
- Inside the Lewinnek zone ≠ guaranteed stable (Azzam) · cup screws → posterosuperior quadrant (→ 6A 6.13)
- Precautions → posterior: no flexion + adduction + IR · lateral: no ER, no crossing legs (Handbook)

PITFALL — cup inclination
- Handbook template → 45° · Lewinnek → 40 ± 10°
- Say → "**about 40–45° inclination, 15° anteversion, combined 30–50°**"

6B.06.b:
### Step by step
| Step | Ganz surgical dislocation |
|---|---|
| Uses | FAI (femoroacetabular impingement), head fractures, SCFE (slipped capital femoral epiphysis) realignment, tumours → 360° view (Campbell) |
| Position | Lateral decubitus; Kocher-Langenbeck or **Gibson** incision (Campbell) |
| Interval | Gibson → anterior border of maximus released, not split (Campbell) |
| Osteotomy | **Trochanteric flip** → posterosuperior greater trochanter edge → posterior vastus ridge, ≤1.5 cm thick, exits in front of the last medius fibres (Campbell) |
| Capsule | **Z-shaped** → along the neck, anteroinferior limb in front of the LT, posterior limb along the labrum (Campbell) |
| Dislocate | Flexion + ER into a sterile bag (Campbell) |

[[FIG: Fig 6B.25 · 6B.06

- Fragment carries medius + minimus above, vastus lateralis below → flipped forward (Hopp)
- **Piriformis and rotators stay** → the deep MFCA is never cut (Gautier 2000; Campbell)

### ETO — extended trochanteric osteotomy
- Lateral third of the femur ("coffin lid") → ≥10 cm from the greater trochanter tip, usually 12–16 cm (Abdel Karim)
- Leave ≥4–6 cm of diaphysis for fixation · round corners · drill before sawing · distal cerclage before reaming (Abdel Karim)
- Uses → infected or loose stem, Vancouver B2, varus remodelled stem (Abdel Karim)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how does Ganz dislocate the hip without killing the head?"
- Trochanteric **flip** osteotomy exits in front of the rotators
- **Rotators intact** → the deep MFCA behind obturator externus survives
- Z capsulotomy with its lower limb **in front of the LT** → MFCA lies just behind-above it
- Dislocate in flexion + ER → full 360° view
- Fix the flip with 2–3 screws (Campbell)

- Uses → infected or loose stem, Vancouver B2, varus remodelled stem (Abdel Karim)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how does Ganz dislocate the hip without killing the head?"
- Trochanteric **flip** osteotomy exits in front of the rotators
- **Rotators intact** → the deep MFCA behind obturator externus survives
- Z capsulotomy with its lower limb **in front of the LT** → MFCA lies just behind-above it
- Dislocate in flexion + ER → full 360° view
- Fix the flip with 2–3 screws (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — medial vs anterior open reduction in DDH (Prof Abdel-Ghani)
